prompt:
An express train travelling at a steady velocity of +32.0 m s^-1 approaches a signal. The driver applies brakes, causing a uniform deceleration of magnitude 1.60 m s^-2 until the train comes to a complete halt.
(a) Calculate the braking distance required for the train to stop. [2]
(b) Calculate the time taken for the train to stop. [1]
(c) Calculate the distance travelled by the train during the first 10.0 s of braking. [1]
hints: Remember that deceleration in the forward direction corresponds to negative acceleration (a = -1.60 m s^-2).
For part (c), substitute t = 10.0 s into s = ut + 0.5 a t^2.
